description: Hand-authored what-if presets. Each one overrides parts of the day's conditions (date, weekday, academic period, weather, events) and runs through the same conditions engine (src/sim/conditions.ts → src/sim/behavior.ts → src/sim/sourceDay.ts). No scenario changes counts or capacities directly; they change people's timelines.

scenarios.label: Ordinary day
scenarios.description: Classes in session, dry and mild, no events. The reference for comparisons.

scenarios.label: Rainy exam week
scenarios.description: Final exams in steady rain: libraries fill, few outings, almost nobody by the river.

scenarios.label: Snow day
scenarios.description: Heavy snow and BU closes: classes cancelled, residents stay in, slow walking.

provenance.note: BU announces weather closures on its emergency page; this date and storm are hypothetical.

scenarios.label: Finals week
scenarios.description: A dry December exam day: exams in place of most classes, long library sessions.

scenarios.label: Heatwave
scenarios.description: Early September, 95°F: indoors at midday, the river in the evening.

scenarios.label: Warm Saturday
scenarios.description: A dry 78°F October Saturday: BU Beach and the Esplanade fill up.

scenarios.label: Home hockey game
scenarios.description: BU men's hockey at Agganis Arena, 7 PM puck drop on a Saturday (a date with no other published event at the arena).

events.label: BU men's hockey at Agganis Arena

provenance.note: Reported attendance at the Oct 10, 2026 home game was 4,951 (goterriers.com box score); about 40% of a crowd that size are assumed to be students. Seats are approximate.

scenarios.label: Move-in day
scenarios.description: The Saturday before fall classes: residents arrive, dining halls busy, no classes.

scenarios.label: Marathon Monday
scenarios.description: Patriots' Day: classes suspended, students head to Kenmore and Beacon Street to cheer.

provenance.note: BU's calendar suspends classes on Patriots' Day (Apr 19, 2027); the Boston Marathon passes Kenmore Square next to campus.
